newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal parties sign controversial reform deal.
newsitem.headline: Portugal parties sign controversial reform deal.

text.p: Portugal's ruling Socialists and the main opposition party on Friday signed a controversial accord for changes to the country's constitution giving emigrants the vote and opening the way to electoral reform.
The accord had triggered an embarrassing row within the ranks of the governing party, with parliamentary deputies accusing their leaders of acting behind their backs.
One proposed change would allow a reduction in the number of members of parliament from their present 230.

Socialist deputies said that they had not been consulted about the move nor about the proposal to give Portuguese emigrants abroad the right to vote in presidential elections, long a demand of the conservative Social Democrats, the principal opposition party.
Critics said that Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, whose party is four seats short of an outright majority in parliament, had conceded too much in negotiations with the Social Democrats.

Socialist deputies only finally agreed to accept the proposals after a late-night meeting with Guterres. But the party's leader in parliament, Jorge Lacao, who headed the negotiating team, was forced to resign on Wednesday because of the row.
The Socialist head of an all-party parliamentary commission on reform also stood down saying that the accord between the two major parties had short-circuited his group's work.

The Socialists and the Social Democrats between them hold 85 percent of parliamentary seats, which means that approval for the reforms, which also include the abolition of compulsory military service, is a foregone conclusion.
The two other parties in parliament, the right-wing Popular Party and the Communists, boycotted the signing ceremony in protest at having been excluded from the negotiations.
